title: Pull surface
tagline: Push and pull a face with a grid of handles; the edges keep G0, G1 or G2 with their neighbours along their whole length.

slides.title: What it does
slides.problem: Onshape has no control-net push/pull. Pull surface puts arrow handles on a face; drag them and a new sheet is built from the face's own control net, with the edge rows locked so it still fits its neighbours.
useWhen: Add a bump or dip to a face
Tweak a surface without rebuilding its curves
slides.caption: P2: +10 mm at the centre of a cylinder patch, G1 edges.

points.head: Locked rows
points.body: 1 / 2 / 3 control-point rows per edge for G0 / G1 / G2: continuity holds along the whole edge.

points.head: Handles
points.body: Free control points move along the normal; the offsets are solved so the surface passes through each handle.

points.head: Enough handles
points.body: G1 needs 5+ handles each way before any is free, G2 7+.

slides.title: The dialog
params: The face to pull (kept; the result is a new sheet).
G0 / G1 / G2 along the edges.
U, V, Offset per handle; filled by dragging; 0 removes.
Iso-curves, keep curves / points, handle grid, offset vectors, print.
Degree (minimum, up to 5); how exactly the face is read.

messages: no handle is free / holes not kept / solve fell back / trimmed edges held approximately

items.head: Counts first
items.body: Changing a count or the continuity resets the offsets; set them before dragging.

items.head: Trims
items.body: Holes are dropped; edges trimmed inside the face hold continuity only approximately.
